objective: Build the smallest cross-platform experiment apparatus that can run equivalent compiled-prompt, native-persistence when available, and TORC continuity lanes using frozen fixtures, thin Codex and Claude Code adapters, deterministic scoring, and verifiable artifacts.
success_evidence: The automated replay suite produces deterministic payloads, scores, and artifact hashes.
Compiled-prompt and TORC lanes complete one real Codex-to-Claude Code readiness smoke.
Native persistence completes through an existing harness feature or is recorded unavailable with probe evidence.
Interrupted and repeated stage execution is idempotent and never transfers TORC authority prematurely.
Every completed run has a valid immutable artifact manifest and deterministic score report.
Windows is verified authoritatively and deterministic replay is verified separately on macOS.
non_goals: Comparative performance conclusions or a claim that TORC beats a baseline.
Provider SDK or direct provider API integration.
A daemon, server, watcher, queue, scheduler, broker, or background worker.
Cross-host authority, synchronization, or production state.
P2 integration with Autowork, Sulis, Bran, Omniroute, agent-mail, lugos-mcp, or HUD.
More than Codex source and Claude Code target live adapters.
Model-based judging, learned scoring, rollback, branching, or lineage merging.
Edits to the parent Lugos repository or its submodule pointer.
accepted_threats: Live harness outputs are nondeterministic even when fixture and settings are fixed.
Harness-reported usage and timing evidence may be absent or incomplete.
Native persistence may be unavailable for a cross-harness transition.
The local single-operator prototype does not defend against a malicious process with filesystem access.
The P1a fixture proves apparatus readiness, not performance on a representative production workload.
